columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Founded 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin; since 2015 Google is a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc.
Handles over 70% of worldwide online search requests, central to most internet users’ experience.
Search works in three stages: crawling (download text, images, video), indexing (analyze and store in a massive index), and serving results (rank and return matches).
Results are personalized by location, search history, and other data; advanced features include exact phrases, file-type and site/domain filters, and AI-powered suggestions.

strengths.title: Primary discovery engine for the entire stack
strengths.detail: Users find courses, newsletters, communities, and content via Google; SEO and rich snippets deeply affect visibility across creator platforms.

strengths.title: Multimodal, high-intent traffic
strengths.detail: Supports queries from troubleshooting and how-tos to product research and local services, ideal for inbound discovery.

strengths.title: Rich tooling for site owners
strengths.detail: Search Console helps measure traffic, fix issues, and optimize visibility (clicks, impressions, indexing, errors).

weaknesses.title: Opaque ranking and frequent changes
weaknesses.detail: Algorithm updates can dramatically change visibility; creators and companies must continually adapt SEO strategies.

weaknesses.title: Ads and AI overviews competing with organic
weaknesses.detail: Ads, knowledge panels, and AI overviews can push organic results lower, reducing click-through even when content ranks.

weaknesses.title: Data privacy and personalization concerns
weaknesses.detail: Heavy personalization relies on user data; some users and businesses worry about tracking and bias.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Google Search is dominant web search engine, crawl, index, and serve results across pages, images, and video, increasingly with AI overviews and multimodal search. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Google Search is a fully automated web search engine that crawls, indexes, and serves web pages, images, videos, and other content to match users’ queries, now increasingly enhanced with AI overviews and multimodal search. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Google Search side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Google Search, this chart does not mark a first-class library job. The product still wins at dominant web search engine, crawl, index, and serve results across pages, images, and video, increasingly with AI overviews and multimodal search. You need to find anything on the open web.
